hero.subtitle_html: Walenstadt → Betlis → Quinten → Weesen — SAC T2 · ~800 m gain · ~18 km one-way · ~6–7 h

intro_html:
The Walensee Höhenweg (Switzerland Mobility route 63) is one of Switzerland's most dramatic cliff traverses: a ~18 km one-way crossing of the near-vertical limestone south shore of Lake Walen (Walensee), connecting Walenstadt in the east to Weesen in the west. For much of the route the path clings to steep cliff faces high above the turquoise lake, with the Churfirsten ridge towering across the water to the north. Fixed ropes assist on the most exposed ledges; the route is rated SAC T2 but demands a firm head for heights.

Midway, the path drops to lake level at Quinten — a car-free hamlet famous for its improbably Mediterranean microclimate: fig trees, palm trees, and a lakeside restaurant reachable only by boat or on foot. After Quinten the route climbs back onto the cliffs before the final descent into Weesen. Return to Walenstadt is by Walensee Schifffahrt boat or a short train ride.
quick_facts: T2 — good path, some exposed ledges with fixed ropes
Yes — steep cliff faces; not suitable for those with severe fear of heights
Car-free village accessible only by boat or on foot; Mediterranean microclimate
Glarus Alps — Glarus (west) / St. Gallen (east section)
Walensee ferry (Weesen → Walenstadt) or train Weesen → Walenstadt (change at Sargans)

getting_there.by_pt_html:
• Train: Zürich HB → Walenstadt (direct IC/IR, ≈45 min). Check sbb.ch.
  • Start hiking from Walenstadt station; trailhead signs are visible from the platform exit.
  • Return from Weesen:
    • Boat (recommended): Walensee Schifffahrt — scenic ~1 h crossing, runs late April–October. Check schedule online.
    • Train: Weesen → Ziegelbrücke → Sargans → Walenstadt (≈40 min + changes).
  • Alternatively: train/boat to Walenstadt and start in reverse from Weesen.
getting_there.by_car_html:
Driving is possible but complicates return logistics on this linear route. Options:

  • Park in Walenstadt (free parking near station), hike to Weesen, return by boat or train.
  • Leave a second car in Weesen (or drop-off) and park the other in Walenstadt.
  • Walenstadt is reached from Zürich via A3 motorway (Sargans exit), ~60 km.

day_plans.footer_html: Start no later than 08:30 in summer to complete comfortably before afternoon thunder risk. Check the boat timetable the night before — afternoon sailings from Weesen are limited outside peak summer season.

day_plans.footer_html: Verify boat departures from Quinten in advance. The ferry does not run in winter (roughly November–March).

lapse_rate.example_html: Example: Walenstadt forecast 15–24 °C → trail high point ≈ 9–18 °C. Wind chill on the exposed clifftops can be significant.

sources_html: MeteoSwiss — use the Walenstadt or Weesen point forecast.
Meteoblue Walenstadt — hourly forecast and wind.
Meteoblue Weesen — western end of the lake.
Thunderstorms are the main risk — the cliffs have no shelter and lightning exposure is high. Turn back or sit out in Quinten if storms build.
weather.season_html: Best season: April – October. This is a low-altitude route (max ~1350 m) so it is often snow-free from April. The south-facing cliffs also dry very quickly after rain. Quinten's microclimate is reliably warm and sheltered. Avoid icy or wet rock on the cliff sections — conditions degrade quickly in autumn rain.

takeaways_html: Crowds: Moderate busy; 40–80 hikers/day typical; weekday solitude achievable.
Microclimate: Thermal updrafts; afternoon wind consistent; lake effect moisture visible.
Ecology shift: Canton boundary vegetation; St. Gallen side more rhododendron; Glarus side rockier.

reports.title: Walensee-Höhenweg: Walenstadt – Weesen
bullets_html: Classic west-to-east traverse, started from Weesen. Strong morning light on the east-facing cliff sections.
Fixed ropes confirmed on the steepest ledges above Betlis — take them seriously on wet rock.
Quinten restaurant packed at noon; arrive before 12:00 or after 13:30 for a table.

reports.title: Walensee Höhenweg — Kletterpfad Quinten
bullets_html: April traverse — cliffs already dry and snow-free, Mediterranean flowers in bloom at Quinten.
Wildflowers exceptional on the south-facing limestone; the route feels more Alpine than the elevation suggests.
Boat from Quinten back to Walenstadt: worth every franc for the lake-level perspective.

reports.title: Walensee-Höhenweg im Herbst
bullets_html: Autumn colours on the cliff vegetation are spectacular; lake reflections are mirror-still.
Caution: damp rock on shaded ledges takes longer to dry than the sun-facing south slopes. Check morning conditions.
Ferry season ends around mid-October — confirm schedule before committing to the boat return.

gear.title: Mandatory
items_html: Sturdy hiking boots (ankle support — path has loose rock and narrow ledges)
2–3 L water (very limited sources on the cliffs; fill at Quinten if passing through early)
Sun protection: hat, sunglasses, SPF 30+ (south-facing cliffs catch all-day sun)
Layers: windproof shell (exposed clifftops can be cold despite low elevation)
Headlamp (if there's any chance of finishing after dark)
Phone with offline SwissTopo or Swisstopo app + GPX track

gear.title: Recommended
items_html: Trekking poles (collapsible — may need stowing on the narrowest ledge sections)
Cash for the Quinten restaurant and ferry ticket
Swimwear — Quinten has a small beach and the lake is swimmable in summer

gear.title: Leave behind
items_html: Heavy pack — this is a long traverse; every kilogram matters on 18 km with 800 m gain
Dogs (not recommended on the exposed ledge sections — steep drops)

safety_html: Ridge exposure: >500m drops; wind >40 km/h = footing risk; no cables.
Cloud formation: Orographic effect; visibility <100m in <10 min.
Descent fatigue: 6–8 hours; lower-limb fatigue increases error risk.
Sun exposure: Limited shade; UV high; protection critical.
Navigation fog: Fog obscures markers; compass/GPS essential.
Turn back if thunderstorms develop — lightning risk above treeline is extreme.
disclaimer_html: Route information compiled from Switzerland Mobility, hikr.org community reports, and Swiss topographic sources. Not professional mountain-safety advice. The Walensee Höhenweg involves genuine clifftop exposure — conditions change rapidly with weather. Always check MeteoSwiss before departure, verify the boat timetable if relying on the ferry return, and honestly assess your comfort with exposed narrow paths before committing to the full traverse. When in doubt, turn back at Quinten.
